script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. MODERN ART GALLERY - DAY

A hushed, elegant space filled with priceless works of art. Canvas after canvas, each one more stunning than the last.

At the center, JAMES (50s, an ambitious art dealer) stands among the patrons, admiring a painting. He wears an expensive suit, a calculating look in his eyes. He turns to his assistant, ANNE (30s, earnest and dedicated), who holds a clipboard.

JAMES
(whispering)
Anne, this one. I want it.

ANNE
Sir, it's already sold.

James' expression darkens.

JAMES
Find out who bought it.

INT. JAMES' OFFICE - LATER

Anne sits at James' large, cluttered desk, poring over sales records. She looks up, finding James standing in the doorway, arms crossed.

ANNE
(nervously)
Sir, I can't find any record of that painting being sold.

JAMES
(angrily)
Liar! You're lying to protect that worthless painting. We need it.

Anne shakes her head.

ANNE
Sir, I'm telling the truth. That painting isn't here.

INT. ART STUDIO - DAY

A chaotic workspace where painters work in silence, brushes in hand. At the center, ELLIOT (40s, a reclusive and brilliant painter) stands before a blank canvas, deep in thought.

Suddenly, there's a knock on the door. Elliot turns to find Anne, who looks uneasy.

ANNE
(nervously)
Mr. Elliot, I need to speak with you about James.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Anne sits across from Elliot, a steaming cup of coffee between them.

ELLIOT
(suspiciously)
What about James?

ANNE
(whispering)
He's trying to buy one of your paintings, but it's already been sold. I think he's lying.

Elliot sighs, rubbing his temples.

ELLIOT
I don't care what James does. That painting isn't for sale.

INT. JAMES' OFFICE - DAY

James sits at his desk, surrounded by stacks of papers. Anne enters, looking worried.

ANNE
(nervously)
Sir, Elliot won't sell the painting.

JAMES
(angrily)
Find another one. We need a new piece for the exhibition.

INT. ART MUSEUM - NIGHT

Anne wanders through the museum, taking in the art around her. She stops in front of a stunning piece, her eyes wide. A security guard approaches.

ANNE
(excitedly)
Sir, may I speak with the curator about this painting?

INT. CURATOR'S OFFICE - NIGHT

Anne sits across from the curator, a distinguished older man.

ANNE
I represent a buyer who's very interested in this painting. May we discuss the sale?

CURATOR
(proudly)
This painting is not for sale. It's a prized part of our collection.

Anne looks disappointed but determined.

ANNE
(persistently)
I understand, but my buyer is willing to make a generous donation to the museum in exchange for the painting.

The curator thinks for a moment, then nods.

CURATOR
Very well. I'll speak with the museum director.

INT. JAMES' OFFICE - DAY

James paces anxiously, a look of frustration on his face. Anne enters, looking triumphant.

ANNE
(excitedly)
Sir, we have a new painting for the exhibition.

JAMES
(relieved)
Which one?

ANNE
It's not one of Elliot's, but it's even better. It's from the museum.

James' expression brightens.

JAMES
(satisfied)
Excellent. Let's go see it.

INT. ART MUSEUM - NIGHT

James and Anne stand before the newly acquired painting, their reflection in the glass case.

JAMES
(smiling)
Anne, this is perfect.

ANNE
(smiling back)
I'm glad you think so, sir.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
